note: A single 0xFF inside a string value. Python's CLI reads the file with path.read_text(encoding='utf-8') and raises UnicodeDecodeError -- it never reaches load_receipt. Node's fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8') substitutes U+FFFD and hands the parser a document that loads, canonicalises and hashes cleanly. So the JavaScript CLI and the browser page verify a file the Python CLI cannot open at all, and the split is one level ABOVE every limit either of them checks: it is in the decoder, not the parser. Worse, see 009.
